findings.title: Interpolation before `isQueryWithRangeVariable` check defeats the guard against splitting `$__range` queries
findings.body: The new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` on line 299 interpolates all template variables (including `$__range`, `$__interval`, etc.) before the `partition` on line 300 calls `querySupportsSplitting`. That function (line 282–288) relies on `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to detect expressions containing `$__range` and exclude them from splitting, because the backend would otherwise interpolate `$__range` with the incorrect sub-range. After interpolation, `$__range` is already replaced with a concrete duration string, so `isQueryWithRangeVariable` returns false and the query is incorrectly classified as splittable. This can produce wrong results for any query using `$__range` in a range selector (e.g., `rate(metric[$__range])`). The interpolation should happen after the splitting eligibility check, or the check should be performed on the original uninterpolated targets.

findings.title: Double interpolation when shard splitting delegates to `runSplitQuery`
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates targets at line 52 via `datasource.applyTemplateVariables`. The interpolated targets are then passed through `splitQueriesByStreamShard` → `runNextRequest` → `runSplitQuery` (line 163), which interpolates them a second time at its own line 299. While often idempotent, this can produce incorrect results if a template variable's resolved value itself contains template syntax (e.g., a variable whose value is `${other_var}`), and it adds unnecessary work on every sub-request. The fix should either skip interpolation in `runSplitQuery` when called from the shard-splitting path (e.g., via an option flag), or remove the early interpolation from `runShardSplitQuery` and rely solely on `runSplitQuery` to interpolate.
